key_insight: OmniCapBench proposes a deeper, more structured way to evaluate audio-visual captioning in multimodal AI. It aims to measure both overall caption quality and fine-grained grounding, revealing where current models still fail.
problem_solved: Existing audio-visual captioning benchmarks force a trade-off between broad coverage and precise localization, while LLM-based judges can be inconsistent. This paper addresses the need for a stable, diagnostic benchmark that can expose fine-grained strengths and weaknesses in multimodal large language models.
method: Introduces OmniCapBench, a deep-structured evaluation framework for fine-grained audio-visual captioning.
Combines global caption evaluation with localized probes to assess both coverage and detailed grounding.
Seeks to reduce reliance on unconstrained LLM judging by using a more controlled benchmark design.
impact: For researchers and practitioners, this benchmark provides a clearer way to test whether multimodal models truly understand audio-visual content or only generate plausible summaries. It can guide model debugging, comparison, and future dataset design.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of global vs. local caption evaluation

paper_title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning
paper_authors: Zhongyu Yang, Jiale Tao, Ruitao Chen, Zuhao Yang, Yingfang Yuan
